subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add an enforceable browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what traffic classes and guarantees should it cover?
rationale: The request adds a public security/config boundary that automation should not define without maintainer intent, especially because hard egress controls and bot-block advisory hints have different guarantees.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific block/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and focused tests against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Make the generic egress-firewall work own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser redirects, subframes, proxy routing, and warnlist behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid claiming enforceable browser denylist coverage and instead surface best-effort known bot-block warnings that do not prevent network access.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-specific block/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and focused tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible history across the browser SSRF config, navigation guard, and docs boundary this decision would extend.
